correctness.rationale: Each stochastic two-state letter matrix acts as an affine interval map f_a(x)=q_a+p_a x with p_a>=0. The maximal terminal coordinate is generated by the nondecreasing upper envelope F (or lower G for state-0 acceptance); its one-dimensional orbit is monotone. Affine comparison signs cannot switch from positive to negative back to positive along a monotone orbit, so unique winning letters have no separated reappearance. For the converse, the explicit f_1(x)=1/4+x/2, eps=2^-(2n+10), crossings c_i=(x_{b_i-1}+x_{b_i})/2 and f_{i+1}=f_i+eps*(x-c_i) give rational stochastic maps with 0<p_i<1, 0<q_i<q_i+p_i<1, increasing orbit staying below 1/2, and unique strict active letter throughout each planned block. A strictly increasing envelope preserves the loss from the first wrong letter. One state cannot distinguish same-length competitors. Independent exact-fraction construction and full competing-word checks of bounded alphabets/run profiles pass; finite testing supports the general symbolic proof.

value.rationale: It exactly classifies a structurally natural family of monotone two-state witnesses for arbitrary finite alphabets and supplies explicit rational constructions involving arbitrarily many distinct symbols. It separates the recognized order-preserving subclass from negative-slope interleaving effects and constitutes meaningful partial structure within the larger-alphabet two-state classification problem.

final_claim: A nonempty word on every finite alphabet of at least two symbols is the unique maximum-acceptance word of an order-preserving (all update slopes nonnegative) two-state probabilistic automaton iff each occurring symbol occupies one contiguous run. Every such word has a rational two-state witness with positive slopes, deterministic start and strict acceptance gap, hence unrestricted A_P(w)=2.
limitations: Order-preserving two-state PFAs only for the iff; no characterization of arbitrary negative-slope PFAs.
Each witness has a positive but word-dependent gap; no uniform gap lower bound.
Full mathematical proof supports arbitrary word lengths; independent finite witnesses are only corroborative.
